title: Type the catch clauses in content_browsing instead of bare catch(e)
why: None of these restrict the caught type, so each also catches Error subtypes (a TypeError from a bad cast, a StateError from a logic bug) and handles them as an ordinary recoverable failure. The sharpest case is cloud_content_service.dart:317 (currently dead per the separate dead-code finding, but worth fixing if kept): if gzip.decode throws for a reason other than 'not gzipped' (e.g. a truncated download), the function returns the still-compressed bytes as valid data, turning a clear decompression failure into a confusing downstream JSON-parse error. text_display_screen.dart:755's bare catch(e, st) around _handleComplete will show 'Could not save' for a genuine programming bug exactly the same way it shows it for an expected write failure.
recommendation: Narrow each to on FormatException/on Exception catch as appropriate; for the gzip fallback specifically, check the gzip magic number (0x1f 0x8b) instead of try/catch.
acceptance_criteria: a grep-based Rule-0 check for '} catch (' without a preceding 'on ' returns zero hits in these 4 files (or dart run custom_lint once its analyzer-9.0 incompatibility, already baselined, is fixed)
